title: Negotiation
completion_message: ¡Implacable! Ahora posees el vocabulario para negociaciones extremas de alto nivel. Sabes identificar tácticas dilatorias, crear ventaja y entregar ultimátums.

parts.visual:
En los niveles más altos del negocio, la negociación es una guerra psicológica. 

1. Brinkmanship (Política al borde del abismo): 
- Empujar una situación peligrosa hasta el límite para hacer que el oponente se rinda. 
Ej: Threatening a nuclear war is the ultimate act of BRINKMANSHIP. 

2. Stonewalling (Dar largas / Obstruccionismo): 
- Retrasar o bloquear intencionalmente una negociación al negarse a cooperar o responder. 
Ej: The union accused the management of STONEWALLING during the talks. 

3. Leverage (Ventaja / Poder de negociación): 
- La ventaja que tienes sobre alguien que te permite forzar su mano. 
Ej: They have no LEVERAGE, so we can dictate the terms of the contract.
parts.audio: Welcome to High-Level Negotiation. At the highest levels of business, negotiation is a psychological war. Number 1: Brinkmanship. Pushing a dangerous situation to the absolute limit in order to make your opponent back down. For example: Threatening a nuclear war is the ultimate act of BRINKMANSHIP. Number 2: Stonewalling. Intentionally delaying or blocking a negotiation by refusing to cooperate, answer questions, or make decisions. For example: The union accused the management of STONEWALLING during the talks. Number 3: Leverage. The power or advantage you hold over someone that allows you to force their hand. For example: They have no LEVERAGE, so we can dictate the terms of the contract.

parts.visual:
4. Ultimatum (Ultimátum): 
- Una demanda final; si no se cumple, habrá consecuencias graves. 
Ej: The CEO issued an ULTIMATUM: return to work by Friday or be fired. 

5. Concession (Concesión): 
- Algo que cedes u otorgas durante una negociación para llegar a un acuerdo. 
Ej: We had to make several CONCESSIONS to close the deal. 

6. Highball / Lowball (Pedir demasiado / Ofrecer muy poco): 
- Empezar una negociación con una oferta ridículamente alta o baja para anclar el precio. 
Ej: I wanted $100k, but they LOWBALLED me with an offer of $50k. 

7. Bluff (Farol / Engañar): 
- Fingir que tienes algo (o harás algo) para asustar al oponente. 
Ej: He threatened to sue us, but I knew he was BLUFFING.
parts.audio: Number 4: Ultimatum. A final demand or statement of terms, the rejection of which will result in retaliation or a breakdown in relations. For example: The CEO issued an ULTIMATUM: return to work by Friday or be fired. Number 5: Concession. Something that you yield or grant during a negotiation to reach an agreement. For example: We had to make several CONCESSIONS to close the deal. Number 6: Highball and Lowball. Starting a negotiation with a ridiculously high demand or low offer to anchor the price. For example: I wanted $100k, but they LOWBALLED me with an offer of $50k. Finally, Number 7: Bluff. To pretend you will do something or that you have an advantage, just to scare your opponent. For example: He threatened to sue us, but I knew he was BLUFFING.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término correcto de negociación extrema.

questions.question: Pushing the negotiations to the absolute limit of breaking down, just to see who blinks first, is called ____.
questions.explanation: Brinkmanship = política al borde del abismo.

questions.question: Every time we ask for financial records, they ignore our emails or make excuses. They are ____ the investigation.
We are the only supplier of this microchip in the world. We have massive ____ over the phone manufacturers. (Ventaja/Poder).
questions.explanation: Leverage = ventaja o poder de negociación.

questions.question: The boss issued an ____: either accept the 10% pay cut or leave the company by tomorrow.
To reach an agreement, both sides must give something up. We must make ____.
I know my car is worth $20,000. Don't ____ me with a ridiculous offer of $5,000.
questions.explanation: Lowball = hacer una oferta inicial insultantemente baja.

questions.question: He says he has another job offer for $200k, but I think he is ____. Let's call his ____. (Faroleando / Ver el farol).
questions.explanation: Bluff = farol. 'Call someone's bluff' es desafiar el farol.

questions.question: A situation in a negotiation where no progress can be made because nobody will compromise is a ____. (Punto muerto).
questions.explanation: Deadlock (o stalemate / impasse) = punto muerto donde nadie avanza.

questions.question: To break the deadlock and reach an agreement is to ____ a deal.
questions.explanation: Strike a deal = cerrar/lograr un trato.

questions.question: If they don't agree to our final price, we will simply ____ away from the deal.
questions.explanation: Walk away = abandonar la negociación (a menudo la mejor táctica).

questions.question: A psychological tactic where one negotiator is friendly and the other is aggressive to confuse the opponent is 'Good Cop, ____ Cop'.
questions.explanation: Good cop, bad cop = policía bueno, policía malo.

questions.question: When you have alternative options if this deal fails, you have a BATNA: Best Alternative to a ____ Agreement.
questions.explanation: BATNA = Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement (tu plan B).

questions.question: To be extremely tough, uncompromising, and ruthless in negotiation is to play ____. (Jugar duro).
questions.explanation: Play hardball = jugar rudo, no ceder, ser agresivo.

questions.question: A small, final demand made right at the end of a negotiation when the opponent is tired and just wants to close is a ____.
questions.explanation: Nibble = el 'mordisquito' (pedir algo pequeño en el último segundo).

questions.question: To agree to a compromise but only if the other side agrees to a totally unrelated demand is to ____ the issues.
questions.explanation: Link the issues = atar/conectar diferentes puntos para negociarlos juntos.

questions.question: An outcome where both sides feel they have gained something and won is a ____-____ situation.
questions.explanation: Win-win situation = donde ambos ganan (ideal en negocios).

questions.question: Setting the initial price ridiculously high to make your later, slightly lower offers look reasonable is called ____.
questions.explanation: Anchoring = el efecto ancla (fijar el primer número en la mente del otro).

questions.question: A condition or term that absolutely cannot be accepted and will kill the negotiation is a deal-____.
To reach an agreement by making concessions. To find a middle ground. We need to ____.
questions.explanation: Compromise = llegar a un acuerdo cediendo.

questions.question: The final, non-negotiable offer. 'Take it or ____ it'.
questions.explanation: Take it or leave it = lo tomas o lo dejas.

questions.question: Acts of ____. (Llevar todo al límite con B)
Stop ____. (Dar largas/Obstruir con S)
We have no ____. (Ventaja/Poder de negociación con L)
Issue an ____. (Ultimátum con U)
Make ____. (Concesiones con C)
Don't ____ me. (Hacer una oferta ridículamente baja con L)
He is ____. (Faroleando con B)
Break the ____. (Punto muerto con D)
Play ____. (Jugar rudo en la negociación con H)
Take it or ____ it. (Lo tomas o lo dejas con L)

pairs.target: Presionar la situación al límite del colapso

Demanda final bajo amenaza de retiro
Algo a lo que renuncias para acordar
Ofrecer un precio absurdamente bajo al inicio
Negociar de manera ruda e implacable
